title: Quantized Transport of Gap Solitons in the Harper-Hofstadter Model
authors: Oliver Ashfield, Henry Davenport, Tom Sheppard, David G. Reid, Holly A. J. Middleton-Spencer, A. C. Berceanu, Frank Schindler, Iacopo Carusotto, Hannah M. Price
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of gap solitons found in the Harper-Hofstadter model with an additional cubic nonlinearity, such as that describing weakly-interacting cold atoms or a Kerr nonlinearity in an optical platform. We find that certain solitons with frequencies deep in the band gap travel with a robust, quantized velocity perpendicular to the applied force and maintain their spatial profile over long timescales. Crucially, this velocity is linearly proportional to the applied force, allowing for arbitrary steering of the nonlinear wavepacket, without breakdown, using only a tunable external force. This quantized transport persists despite a highly non-uniform occupation of the linear Bloch states, and contrasts with solitons near the band edge, which deform and delocalize under the same force. These results point to a robust and highly controllable mechanism for steering nonlinear solitons in experimentally accessible platforms.
summary: This paper analyzes gap solitons in the nonlinear Harper-Hofstadter model to demonstrate a robust, quantized transport mechanism. Mid-gap solitons exhibit a velocity perpendicular to the applied force that is linearly proportional to the force, enabling precise, controllable steering. This contrasts sharply with band-edge solitons, which become unstable under the same driving force.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamics and transport of gap solitons in the nonlinear Harper-Hofstadter model when subjected to an external force.
main_result: Gap solitons with frequencies deep within the band gap exhibit a robust, quantized velocity perpendicular to the applied force, which is linearly proportional to the force and allows for arbitrary steering.
method: The analysis involves numerically solving the nonlinear evolution equation and analyzing the center-of-mass motion by fitting the position evolution to an ideal quantized trajectory.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the Harper-Hofstadter model, which describes particle hopping on a 2D lattice under a magnetic field, augmented with a cubic nonlinearity (e.g., for cold atoms or Kerr optics).
key_observables: Quantized transverse velocity ($v_{\perp}$), Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR) for localization, and the center-of-mass position $r_{\perp}(t)$.
important_parameters: Soliton frequency ($\omega$) relative to the band gap, the strength of the external force ($F$), and the Chern number ($C_i$) of the underlying bands.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the quantized motion is robust and can be characterized by fitting the position evolution to a specific functional form derived from the external force.
figures_summary: Figures compare the perpendicular motion of band-edge versus mid-gap solitons under force, demonstrating the robust, quantized motion for mid-gap solitons, and show the fitting of the center-of-mass trajectory to the ideal quantized curve.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the model (Harper-Hofstadter with nonlinearity), contrasting the unstable motion of band-edge solitons with the stable, quantized transport of mid-gap solitons, and finally quantifying this robust steering mechanism.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable mechanism for steering nonlinear wavepackets in systems relevant to quantum optics and cold atoms, linking transport properties directly to the topological invariants (Chern numbers) of the underlying band structure.
